Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the detailed questions from your security and infra teams. Per our conversation, I wanted to surface the key items and next steps related to telemetry, PII handling, and subprocessors so your legal and security teams have what they need for the procurement timeline.

Quick recap and what I attached:
- Subprocessors: attached PDF (redwood_subprocessor_list_v1.pdf) lists our current third parties (cloud providers, observability vendors, analytics).
- Telemetry fields: attached CSV (telemetry_data_fields.csv) maps which telemetry/metrics contain no PII, which contain metadata, and retention defaults.
- Data residency: hosted offering stores logs and request metadata in the region you select; full data residency (control plane in your VPC) is available via our Private deployment.

Requested follow-ups (next steps):
1) Legal: review attached subprocessors list and flag any vendor you require us to remove or substitute (Tom Reed noted a specific concern about telemetry vendor X).
2) Security: confirm whether the default 90-day telemetry retention is acceptable or if you need shorter retention (we can offer 30/7-day profiles via Dedicated).
3) Product/Infra: If you need KV-cache traces redacted from logs, we can enable richer redaction and provide sample logs.

Timeline: if legal confirms subprocessors by Tuesday (10/20), we can get an updated SOW/SLA with the vendor appendix and send a DocuSign draft.

If it helps I can also loop in our privacy/security SME (Dev) for a quick call to go through the telemetry fields live.

Thanks —

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the materials and the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side after initial review:

- Telemetry vendor X (listed as an analytics/subscriptions vendor) is a potential blocker for us — our security team needs confirmation that no request body or PII is ever sent to that vendor. Can you confirm the telemetry schema and whether any request identifiers or user_ids are forwarded?
- Retention: legal's default ask is 30 days for telemetry logs related to production requests unless otherwise justified. Is that a hard limit for hosted customers, or is it configurable per account?
- Subprocessor audit: legal requests a timeline and process for notification if you add a new subprocessor in future (we need 30 days notice and an ability to object).

Can you route these to Dev/security and get back to us? Also copy any contract/appendix language you would propose so we can start drafting internal comments.

Marissa / team —

Saw Samantha's questions. Quick answers we can share with FinServ:

- Telemetry vendor behavior: We only send aggregated metrics and anonymized event counters to our telemetry vendor; request bodies and raw prompts are never forwarded. The telemetry_data_fields.csv shows the exact fields we forward. We can also offer an allowlist/denylist so customer-specific identifiers (user_id, email) are redacted before export.
- Retention: Hosted default for telemetry is 90 days, but we support configurable retention windows down to 7 days on Dedicated and 30 days as a standard configurable option for hosted accounts upon request. We can commit to 30-day retention for this account in the SOW.
- Subprocessor notification: Standard policy is 30 days' notice for material changes with an escalation path; we can include an explicit objection and substitution clause in the appendix (sample language below).

Suggested contract language (for legal to review):
"Redwood will provide written notice of any addition of subprocessors at least thirty (30) days prior to such change. Customer will have the right to object to a new subprocessor on the basis of reasonable data protection or security concerns. If Customer objects, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide an alternative subprocessor or mitigation measures."

I'll attach a redline-ready appendix. Recommend we propose 30-day retention and allowlist-based telemetry exports as part of the SOW.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Security & Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
